college: Northbridge College of Engineering & Technology (fictional sample institution)

entries.action: Share admission brochure and eligibility criteria
entries.question: What is the eligibility for B.Tech admission?
alt_questions: minimum marks required for engineering admission
entries.answer: Candidates must have passed Class 12 (HSC) with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects plus one of Chemistry, Biology, Biotechnology or Computer Science, with at least 45% aggregate (40% for reserved categories). A valid score in MHT-CET or JEE Main is required. Admission is through the state CAP rounds and the institute-level quota.

entries.action: Guide applicant through online application portal
entries.question: How do I apply for admission?
entries.answer: Register on the admissions portal (admissions.northbridge.edu), fill in the online application form, upload scanned documents, and pay the non-refundable application fee of Rs. 1,000. After the merit list is published, confirm your seat by reporting to the Admissions Office with original documents within the deadline shown on the portal.

entries.question: Which documents are required at the time of admission?
alt_questions: what papers do I need to bring for admission
entries.answer: Bring originals and two attested copies of: Class 10 and 12 mark sheets, CET/JEE score card, School Leaving / Transfer Certificate, domicile certificate, caste certificate and caste validity (if applicable), non-creamy layer certificate (if applicable), income certificate (for fee concession), Aadhaar card, 4 passport-size photographs, and a gap certificate if there is a gap in education.

entries.question: Is direct second year (lateral entry) admission available for diploma holders?
alt_questions: diploma to degree direct second year
entries.answer: Yes. Diploma holders with at least 45% (40% for reserved categories) can join the second year of B.Tech through the Direct Second Year (DSE) CAP process conducted by the state. Up to 10% of intake plus vacancies from first year are available for lateral entry.

entries.action: Share list of programmes and intake
entries.question: Which courses and branches are offered?
alt_questions: what programmes does the college offer
entries.answer: The college offers B.Tech in Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence & Data Science, Electronics & Telecommunication, Mechanical Engineering and Civil Engineering, plus M.Tech in Computer Engineering and VLSI, and an MBA programme. Each B.Tech branch has an intake of 120 except Civil (60).

entries.action: Process admission cancellation as per refund policy
entries.question: How do I cancel my admission and get a refund?
entries.answer: Submit the admission cancellation form at the Admissions Office along with the original fee receipt and a cancelled cheque. If you cancel before the last CAP round cut-off date, the full fee minus a processing charge of Rs. 1,000 is refunded. After that date, refunds follow the state fee regulating authority rules and depend on whether the seat is filled. Refunds are processed within 30 working days.

entries.question: What is the fee structure for B.Tech?
alt_questions: how much is the tuition fee
entries.answer: For 2026-27 the B.Tech fee is Rs. 1,25,000 per year (tuition Rs. 1,10,000 + development Rs. 15,000). Exam fees of Rs. 1,800 per semester and a one-time caution deposit of Rs. 5,000 (refundable) are charged separately. Hostel and transport fees are extra.

entries.action: Explain online and offline payment options
entries.question: How can I pay my college fees?
entries.answer: Fees can be paid online through the student ERP portal (UPI, net banking, debit/credit card) or by demand draft in favour of 'Northbridge College of Engineering' payable at Pune. Cash is not accepted. Download the e-receipt from the ERP portal after payment.

entries.question: My semester fee was deducted but the portal still shows unpaid. What should I do?
alt_questions: money debited but fee status not updated
entries.answer: Online payments can take up to 48 hours to reconcile. If the status is still unpaid after 48 hours, email accounts@northbridge.edu with your enrollment number, the transaction reference/UTR number, date, amount and a screenshot of the bank debit. The Accounts team verifies the transaction with the payment gateway and updates your status within 3 working days. If the payment actually failed, the bank auto-reverses the amount within 5-7 working days.

entries.question: Can I pay the fees in instalments?
entries.answer: Yes. Students can apply for a two-instalment plan by submitting a written request to the Accounts Office before the fee due date. The first instalment (60%) is paid at the start of the year and the second (40%) before 15 January. A late fee applies if the second instalment is delayed.

entries.action: Inform about late fee and waiver request
entries.question: What is the late fee for delayed payment?
entries.answer: A late fee of Rs. 50 per day is charged after the due date, up to a maximum of Rs. 5,000. Students with genuine hardship can request a waiver from the Registrar with supporting documents. Unpaid fees can block exam hall tickets and result access.

entries.action: Guide student to download fee receipt
entries.question: How do I get my fee receipt?
entries.answer: Log in to the student ERP portal, open Fees > Payment History, and click Download Receipt for the relevant transaction. For a stamped duplicate receipt, apply at the Accounts Office window (10 AM - 4 PM) with your ID card.

entries.question: How do I get my caution deposit back?
entries.answer: The Rs. 5,000 caution deposit is refunded after you graduate or leave the college. Submit the No Dues form signed by the Library, Hostel, Department and Accounts along with a cancelled cheque. The refund is credited to the bank account within 45 days.

entries.action: Share scholarship schemes and portal link
entries.question: What scholarships are available?
entries.answer: Students can apply for government scholarships on the MahaDBT portal (Post-Matric scholarship, EBC fee reimbursement, Rajarshi Shahu Maharaj scholarship, minority scholarships) and the National Scholarship Portal. The college also offers merit scholarships: 50% tuition waiver for the top 3 rankers of each branch, and need-based aid for family income below Rs. 2.5 lakh per year.

entries.action: Check application status on MahaDBT and escalate
entries.question: My scholarship has not been credited yet. What should I do?
entries.answer: First check your application status on the MahaDBT / NSP portal. Make sure your bank account is Aadhaar-seeded and DBT-enabled. If the status shows 'Pending at college', contact the Scholarship Cell (Room A-104) with your application ID. If it is pending at the government level, the college cannot speed it up, but the Scholarship Cell can raise a grievance on your behalf.

entries.question: What is the last date to apply for scholarships?
entries.answer: The MahaDBT portal usually opens in October and closes in January, but dates are set by the government each year. The Scholarship Cell posts the exact dates on the notice board and student ERP. Submit the printed application and documents to the Scholarship Cell within 7 days of online submission.

entries.question: What is the examination and evaluation pattern?
entries.answer: Each theory course is evaluated out of 100: 30 marks Continuous Internal Evaluation (two class tests and assignments) and 70 marks End Semester Examination. Labs are evaluated through term work and practical/oral exams. The grading uses a 10-point CGPA scale.

entries.action: Check fee and attendance status, release hall ticket
entries.question: I cannot download my exam hall ticket. What should I do?
entries.answer: Hall tickets are released on the student ERP portal 7 days before exams. A hall ticket is withheld if fees are pending, attendance is below 75%, or the exam form was not submitted. Clear any dues and visit the Examination Cell (Room B-012) with your ID card; they will verify and release the hall ticket.

entries.question: How do I apply for revaluation or photocopy of my answer sheet?
entries.answer: Apply on the ERP portal within 7 days of result declaration. Photocopy of answer sheet costs Rs. 300 per course and revaluation costs Rs. 500 per course. You must request the photocopy first; revaluation can be applied for within 5 days of receiving it. Revised results are published within 30 days.

entries.question: How do I clear a backlog (KT) subject?
entries.answer: Failed courses can be cleared in the supplementary examination held in June/July or in the next regular examination. Fill the backlog exam form on the ERP portal with a fee of Rs. 500 per course. Under ATKT rules you may proceed to the next year with backlogs only if you have not failed more than the permitted number of courses for that year (see the academic rulebook).

entries.question: When will semester results be declared?
entries.answer: Results are generally declared within 45 days of the last examination and are published on the ERP portal under Examination > Results. Grade cards are distributed by the department about two weeks after declaration.

entries.question: I missed an exam due to illness. Can I appear again?
entries.answer: For a missed class test, submit a medical certificate to your department within 3 days to request a re-test. For a missed end-semester exam, there is no separate re-exam; you appear in the supplementary exam. With a valid medical certificate from a registered doctor submitted within 7 days, the Examination Cell waives the backlog exam fee.

entries.question: How do I convert CGPA to percentage?
entries.answer: As per the affiliating university rule, Percentage = (CGPA - 0.75) x 10. For example, a CGPA of 8.25 equals 75%. The Examination Cell can issue an official conversion certificate on request.

entries.question: What is the minimum attendance requirement?
entries.answer: Students must have at least 75% attendance in each course (theory and lab separately) to be eligible for the end-semester exam. Attendance shortage up to 10% may be condoned by the Principal for documented medical reasons or approved college activities.

entries.action: Process duty leave for approved activity
entries.question: How do I get attendance for participating in events or competitions?
entries.answer: Apply for Duty Leave (OD) through your class teacher before the event, attaching the invitation/registration proof. After the event, submit the participation certificate within 5 days. Approved OD days are counted as present.

entries.question: Where can I find the academic calendar?
entries.answer: The academic calendar is on the college website under Academics > Calendar and on the ERP dashboard. For 2026-27, the odd semester runs from 1 August to 5 December and the even semester from 5 January to 20 May. Winter break is 20 December to 4 January.

entries.question: How do I choose my elective subjects?
entries.answer: Elective registration opens on the ERP portal two weeks before the semester. Choose your preferences in order; seats are allotted on a first-come, CGPA-based basis. Each elective needs at least 20 students to run. Changes are allowed only in the first week of the semester with the HoD's approval.

entries.question: Can I change my branch after first year?
entries.answer: Branch change is allowed only after the first year, based on first-year CGPA (minimum 7.5, no backlogs) and availability of vacant seats in the requested branch. Applications open in July on the ERP portal. Branch change is not allowed for lateral entry students.

entries.question: Is an internship compulsory?
entries.answer: Yes. Every B.Tech student must complete an internship of at least 8 weeks (can be split into two 4-week internships) before the end of the seventh semester. It carries 4 credits. Submit the offer letter, completion certificate and report to your department's internship coordinator.

entries.action: Guide student to mentor and HoD
entries.question: Who is my mentor and how do I contact them?
entries.answer: Every student is assigned a faculty mentor for the full programme. Your mentor's name and email are shown on the ERP dashboard under My Profile > Mentor. Mentor meetings happen at least twice a semester; you can also book a slot by email.

entries.question: What are the library timings?
entries.answer: The central library is open 8 AM to 9 PM on weekdays and 9 AM to 5 PM on Saturdays. During exam periods it stays open until 11 PM and on Sundays from 9 AM to 5 PM. The reading hall is open 24x7 during exam weeks.

entries.question: How many books can I borrow and for how long?
entries.answer: UG students can borrow up to 4 books for 14 days; PG students up to 6 books for 21 days. Books can be renewed twice online through the library OPAC if there is no reservation. Reference books and journals cannot be taken out.

entries.question: What is the fine for late return or a lost book?
entries.answer: The overdue fine is Rs. 2 per day per book. For a lost book, you must replace it with the same or latest edition, or pay twice the current price of the book plus a processing fee of Rs. 100. Report the loss to the circulation desk as soon as possible to stop the fine from increasing.

entries.question: How do I access e-books and IEEE journals from home?
entries.answer: The college subscribes to IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Springer, NPTEL and DELNET. Use the remote access portal (elib.northbridge.edu) with your college email ID. On campus, access is automatic over the college Wi-Fi.

entries.question: Is hostel accommodation available and what does it cost?
entries.answer: Separate hostels are available for boys (400 seats) and girls (300 seats). The 2026-27 hostel fee is Rs. 75,000 per year for a triple-sharing room and Rs. 90,000 for double-sharing, including mess charges (4 meals a day), Wi-Fi, laundry and 24x7 security. Allotment is based on distance from home and merit.

entries.question: How do I apply for the hostel?
entries.answer: Apply through the ERP portal under Hostel > New Application within 7 days of confirming admission. Upload a medical fitness certificate, parent consent form and two photographs. The allotment list is published within 10 days; pay the hostel fee within 5 days of allotment to keep the room.

entries.question: What are the hostel in-time and leave rules?
alt_questions: going home on weekend from hostel
entries.answer: Hostel in-time is 9:30 PM for all residents. For overnight leave or going home, submit a leave request on the hostel app with parent approval at least one day in advance. Late entry without permission is recorded and repeated violations are reported to parents.

entries.question: There is a problem with water, electricity or furniture in my hostel room. Whom should I contact?
entries.answer: Raise a maintenance complaint on the hostel app or in the complaint register at the warden's office. Electrical and plumbing issues are attended within 24 hours; furniture within 3 days. For emergencies (no water, power failure, safety issues) call the hostel warden helpline at extension 2200 immediately.

entries.question: How can I give feedback about mess food?
entries.answer: A mess committee with student representatives meets every month. Submit feedback on the hostel app or in the mess feedback register. Hygiene or food-safety issues should be reported to the warden immediately.

entries.question: What is the eligibility for campus placements?
entries.answer: Final-year students who have registered with the Training & Placement Cell are eligible. Most companies require a minimum CGPA of 6.5 and no active backlogs at the time of the drive. Students who accept one offer can apply only to 'dream' companies offering at least 1.5 times their current package.

entries.question: How do I register for placements?
entries.answer: Register on the T&P portal (placements.northbridge.edu) at the start of the seventh semester. Upload your resume, mark sheets and a photograph, and pay the registration fee of Rs. 500. Drive notifications are sent via email and the portal; check them daily.

entries.question: What were the placement statistics last year?
entries.answer: For the 2025-26 batch, 86% of eligible students were placed. The highest package was Rs. 32 LPA, the average was Rs. 6.8 LPA, and 140 companies visited, including TCS, Infosys, Accenture, Persistent, Bosch, L&T and several product startups.

entries.question: Does the college provide placement training?
entries.answer: Yes. The T&P Cell runs aptitude, coding and soft-skills training from the fifth semester, plus mock interviews and resume reviews in the seventh semester. Sessions are held on Saturdays and are mandatory for students who want to sit for placements.

entries.question: I forgot my ERP portal password. How do I reset it?
entries.answer: Click 'Forgot Password' on the ERP login page and enter your enrollment number; a reset link is sent to your registered college email. If you no longer have access to the email, visit the IT Help Desk (Room C-201) with your ID card or email ithelpdesk@northbridge.edu from your personal email with a photo of your ID card.

entries.question: How do I connect to the campus Wi-Fi?
entries.answer: Connect to the 'NB-Student' network and log in with your college email ID and ERP password. Each student can register up to 2 devices. If you cannot connect, forget the network and reconnect, or visit the IT Help Desk.

entries.action: Explain college email and software licences
entries.question: How do I get my college email ID and free software like Microsoft Office?
entries.answer: Your college email (enrollmentnumber@student.northbridge.edu) is created within a week of admission; the initial password is sent to your registered mobile number. With it you get free Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, GitHub Student Developer Pack eligibility and campus licences for MATLAB and AutoCAD.

entries.action: Share bus routes and pass fee
entries.question: Does the college provide bus facility?
entries.answer: Yes. College buses run on 12 routes across the city. The annual bus pass costs Rs. 18,000 to Rs. 24,000 depending on the route distance. Apply on the ERP portal under Transport; route maps and timings are on the college website.

entries.action: Guide student for student concession pass
entries.question: How do I get a railway or bus concession pass?
entries.answer: Collect the railway/state transport concession form from the Student Section after filling the request on the ERP portal. It is issued within 2 working days with the college stamp. You need a valid college ID card.

entries.question: How do I get a bonafide certificate?
alt_questions: student certificate for passport or bank
entries.answer: Apply on the ERP portal under Student Services > Bonafide Certificate, mentioning the purpose (bank loan, passport, scholarship, etc.). The fee is Rs. 50. The certificate is ready for collection at the Student Section within 2 working days.

entries.question: How do I apply for official transcripts?
entries.answer: Apply on the ERP portal under Student Services > Transcripts. The fee is Rs. 1,000 for the first set and Rs. 300 for each additional set. Transcripts are issued in sealed envelopes within 10 working days. For WES/ECA, mention the reference number and the college will courier them directly (courier charges extra).

entries.action: Process leaving certificate after no dues
entries.question: How do I get my Leaving Certificate (LC) or Transfer Certificate?
entries.answer: Submit the No Dues form signed by all departments and the LC application at the Registrar Office. The LC is issued within 5 working days. Original documents submitted at admission are returned along with it.

entries.action: Process duplicate ID card or mark sheet
entries.question: I lost my ID card or mark sheet. How do I get a duplicate?
entries.answer: For a duplicate ID card, apply at the Student Section with a Rs. 200 fee; it is issued in 3 days. For a duplicate mark sheet, submit a police complaint/lost report copy, an affidavit on Rs. 100 stamp paper and a fee of Rs. 500 per mark sheet at the Examination Cell; it takes about 15 working days.

entries.action: Share convocation and degree certificate details
entries.question: When and how will I receive my degree certificate?
entries.answer: Degree certificates are awarded by the affiliating university at the annual convocation, usually held in February-March. Register for convocation on the university portal when notified. Students who do not attend can collect the degree certificate from the Registrar Office afterwards.

entries.question: How do I report ragging?
entries.answer: Ragging is a criminal offence and is strictly prohibited on campus. Report it immediately to the Anti-Ragging Squad helpline (extension 1100 / +91-20-5550-1100), any member of the Anti-Ragging Committee, or the national anti-ragging helpline 1800-180-5522 (antiragging.in). Complaints are confidential and action begins within 24 hours.

entries.action: Register grievance and assign to committee
entries.question: How do I submit a complaint or grievance?
entries.answer: Submit your grievance on the ERP portal under Grievance or drop a written complaint in the grievance box outside the Principal's office. The Student Grievance Redressal Committee acknowledges complaints within 2 working days and resolves them within 15 days. You can escalate unresolved issues to the university ombudsperson.

entries.question: Is there a counsellor I can talk to about stress or mental health?
entries.answer: Yes. A professional counsellor is available free of charge in the Student Wellness Centre (Room A-210), Monday to Saturday, 10 AM to 5 PM. Book a confidential appointment via wellness@northbridge.edu or walk in. If you are in immediate distress, contact the Tele-MANAS helpline 14416 (24x7) or the campus emergency number.

entries.question: How do I report sexual harassment?
entries.answer: Contact the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) at icc@northbridge.edu or meet the ICC presiding officer in Room A-110. Complaints are handled confidentially under the POSH Act and UGC regulations. Interim relief, such as changing class sections, can be arranged during the inquiry.

entries.action: Direct student to medical centre / emergency
entries.question: Is there a medical facility on campus?
entries.answer: The campus Medical Centre near Gate 2 has a doctor from 9 AM to 6 PM and a nurse 24x7. An ambulance is available round the clock (extension 1000). All students are covered by group medical insurance of Rs. 1 lakh per year through the college.

entries.question: What sports facilities are available?
entries.answer: The campus has a cricket and football ground, basketball and volleyball courts, a badminton hall, table tennis, chess and a gym (6-9 AM and 5-8 PM). Students can join college teams through trials held in August.

entries.question: How do I join a student club?
entries.answer: Clubs recruit during the Club Fair in the second week of August. Active clubs include the Coding Club, Robotics Club, AI & ML Club, IEEE Student Branch, GDG on Campus, NSS, Drama, Music and Photography. Join via the club's form on the Student Activities page.

entries.question: What are the college office timings and contact details?
entries.answer: The administrative office is open Monday to Saturday, 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM (closed on second and fourth Saturdays). Address: Northbridge College of Engineering & Technology, Hinjewadi Road, Pune 411057. Phone: +91-20-5550-1000. Email: info@northbridge.edu.

entries.action: Explain ID card and dress code rules
entries.question: Is there a dress code and is the ID card compulsory?
entries.answer: Wearing the college ID card is compulsory on campus. There is no uniform, but students must wear formal clothes on Mondays and for placement activities, and safety shoes and lab coats in workshops and labs.

entries.question: Are there student exchange or study abroad programmes?
entries.answer: The International Relations Office has semester exchange agreements with partner universities in Germany, Japan and Australia. Students with a CGPA of 8.0 or above can apply in their fifth semester. Credits earned abroad are transferred under the credit transfer policy.
